《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月12日，星期五

昨夜提篮桥路（Tifeng Rd.）出现不安局势

五十名强力人员守卫；今日将提出抗议

昨夜深夜，提篮桥路（Tifeng Rd.）沿线“路障区域”的居民中出现了一定的不安情绪。从上海公共租界警务处深夜获得的一份报告表明，一些居民正试图从家中搬往更为适宜的住处。

守卫的警察分队有所加强，至午夜时分，在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）与愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）之间的提篮桥路上，有50名华捕巡长和10名外籍警官执勤。所有行动均由静安寺路捕房指挥，该捕房在回应查询时反复发布“一切平静”的报告。

昨晚获悉，出于命运的捉弄，上海公共租界警务处一名外籍侦探的寓所恰位于受影响区域。这并不意味着该外籍警官拖欠税款，他只是受普遍路障影响的众多人员之一。昨夜深夜发布的中文报告甚至坚称，在96户被路障封锁的家庭中，仅有20户拖欠税款。

据悉，第一特区市民联合会第三十四支会这一强有力的华人组织，将根据收到的大量请愿书的要求，于今日召开紧急会议讨论此问题：

关于此前局势的详细报道见本期第4版。

page_data.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, MARCH 12, 1937

Barricaded Tenements In
Western District Under
Close S.M. Police Guard

Over One Hundred Houses On Tifeng Road Have
Been Prevented From Access To Settlement Roads;
Municipal Authorities Block Sewage Outlet

TENANTS OF HOUSES REMAIN CALM BUT
EXPRESS INDIGNATION AT ACTION

As the result of the positive action of the Municipal Police,
under the direction of the Shanghai Municipal Council, the
tenants of more than one hundred foreign-style houses on Tifeng
Road were cut off from direct access to Municipal roads early
yesterday morning. Further definite action against the house-
holders was taken when the Public Works Department stopped
the sewage outlet from the block of buildings.

As was first pointed out by "The Shanghai Times" yester-
day morning, police from the Bubbling Well Station, assisted
by P.W.D. coolies, barricaded the entrances to several blocks of
buildings on the Western side of Tifeng Road, extending from
Yu Yuen Road to Bubbling Well Road. Lanes leading from
these dwellings to Tifeng, Bubbling Well and Yu Yuen Roads
were effectively closed to all traffic. Residents had either to
emerge on Settlement roads through shop entrances or make
their way along a Chinese-owned lane at the rear of the
premises.

In every respect the police
blockade was effective yesterday.
Heavy, specially constructed wooden
structures topped by strands of
barbed wire placed too high for suc-
cessful scaling were thrown across
the eleven entrances to the rows
of buildings. Every outlet was
thoroughly blocked and police
stationed at each barricade to
prevent any attempts on the part
of those inside to attempt forceful
removal of the barriers or any other
untoward move.

District Quiet

But there was a general quiet
over the entire neighbourhood.
Those residing behind the barri-
cades resigned themselves to the
situation and found their way to
the Settlement main roads either
through several shops located at the
corner of Tifeng and Yu Yuen Roads,
or walked down a narrow alley
leading from the rear of the little
colony to Yu Yuen Road.

Naturally there was considerable
indignation among the tenants of
the buildings. But, in view of the
fact that the barricading had been
speedily and effectively carried out
when the majority of residents were
asleep or indoors, no attempt was
made to interfere with the work of
the police or coolie staffs. Further-
more, action of some such character
had been repeatedly threatened by
Municipal officials and it came as
no great surprise to those now
affected.

Shortly after daylight yesterday
morning a gang of P. W. D. work-

men commenced digging at the Yu
Yuen Road entrance to the buildings
and, in a short time, had cut off the
sewer outlet from the property to
the main sewerage system of the
S. M. C. So far there has been no
attempt made or threat offered that
the light, water or telephone
services will be cut, but there is
nothing at present to guarantee that
these steps might not be taken if
the tenants continue obdurate.

Refuse To Pay

The steps which have been taken
by the Council in connection with
residents in the barricaded area
followed the continual refusal of
these tenants of some 105 houses to
pay the municipal rates. The house
occupiers on this property are
obliged to pay their own rates and
these are not included in the rentals.
Some, but only a very few, have
paid these dues. The remainder
have persistently refused.

Driven to the point where some
action had to be taken to enforce
its demands, the Shanghai Municipal
Council planned the barricading of
the entire property and this was
carried out early yesterday morn-
ing. In bitterly cold weather and
pouring rain squads of Chinese
coolies shepherded and guarded by
detachments of police from Bubbl-
ing Well Station and the Reserve
Unit, rapidly transferred the bar-
ricades from nearby depots to the
points where they are now erected.
The utmost secrecy had been
observed by officials and the
neighbourhood was taken by
surprise.

Warning, however, had been
given the tenants that they could
remove their cars before a stipulat-
ed hour if they desired to do so,
but quite a number of them, imag-
ining that it was only another
gesture on the part of the S.M.C.,
decided to take the risk. Their
cars are now unable to reach the
main roads.

Police Stand By

Throughout the night and all day
yesterday police detachments were
on duty at the various entrances.
They will remain there in reliefs
until the Council obtains satisfac-
tion from the tenants. The only
buildings in the barricaded area
which have direct access to the
Settlement roads are several shops,
the entrances to which have not
been effected. Many of the inside
tenants are using shops to enter and
leave the besieged zone.

The property involved is official-
ly located at 361 Yu Yuen Road, but
it extends from that road along
Tifeng Road as far as Bubbling
Well Road, with considerable depth.
There are ten terraces of three-
storeyed foreign-style dwellings,
separated by lanes sufficiently wide

BARRICADES ON TIFENG ROAD

Residents of Lane 361, Yu Yuen Road awoke with a start yester-
day morning to find that all their Tifeng Road and Bubbling Well
Road lane entrances had been blocked by the Shanghai Municipal
Police. Designated as "Municipal amenities," the roads are held by the
Council to be for the use of only those ratepayers who help to swell
the municipal coffers. The photograph at top shows a general view
of the barricades, while below is shown several of the police on duty.
[Ah Fong

to permit motor traffic. It is these
lanes, having access to Tifeng Road,
Yu Yuen Road and Bubbling Well
Road, which have been blockaded.
At either end of the property
several shop frontages are located.
Those on Bubbling Well Road are
vacant, but those opposite the
Bubbling Well Fire Station, on Yu
Yuen Road, are doing business. The
property was erected in 1932 and
is Chinese owned.

Warning Ignored

A warning regarding the non-
payment of rates was addressed to
all residents of this area by Mr.
V. H. Bourne, Deputy Treasurer,
but this was ignored. A further
warning and an ultimatum was de-
livered a few days ago, the tenants
were informed that unless payment
was made access to Municipal roads
would be stopped and the sewer
system discontinued.

It is difficult to know how many
people reside in the affected area,
but it was learned yesterday that
there were only only two foreign-
ers in residence there.

Questioned yesterday, officials of
the Council stated emphatically that
they would not remove the barri-
cades nor restore the sewerage con-
nection until the tenants had paid
their rates. The Council indicated
determination to carry on an in-
definite siege. It was also hinted
that steps in other districts along
Settlement Roads, where rates had
been withheld, would be carried
out on similar lines wherever it was
deemed necessary.

Revenue Department officials
last evening declined to name in
round figures that amount of rates
involved in the present case, but
stated it was considerable. The
situation on the outside roads in the
past few years has gone from bad
to worse so far as revenue is con-
cerned. More and more residents
have refused to pay and the loss
to the S. M. C. is enormous.

The protracted negotiations for a
settlement of the disputed right to

control these thoroughfares and tax
the residents thereon is no nearer.
Discussions between Mr. Stirling
Fessenden of the S. M. C. and Mr.
O. K. Yui, of the Shanghai City
Government, reached a point where
a modus vivendi was drawn up. But
that is as far as the negotiations
got. All efforts since to seek a way
out of the impasse have proved
fruitless.

In the meantime, the majority of
residents on these roads are escap-
ing taxation to a large extent, pay-
ing neither to the Chinese on the
one hand and refusing payment to
the Settlement authorities on the
other.

"Defaulter's" View

Resignation rather than indigna-
tion was expressed to "The Shang-
hai Times" yesterday by one of the
Chinese residents in Tifeng Road,
and a self-confessed "defaulter."
"In a way, we are glad that the
Council has taken action," he de-
clared, "for now the problem of
rates should be settled once and
for all."

The resident, a businessman who
is well-known in the city, declared
that the "defaulters" were less to
blame than the authorities involved,
who had permitted the situation to
reach its present state of
uncertainty.

"On the one hand we are approach-
ed by S. M. C. collectors," he
explained, "and if we don't pay
them, then there is inevitably a
good deal of unpleasantness. And
on the other hand, we are dunned
by Chinese tax collectors—who, if
they are not satisfied, are just as
unpleasant.

"This means that unless we pay
double taxes, we get a portion of
trouble one way or the other, so
who can blame us for refusing to
pay at all until the situation has
become clarified? Given an author-
itative ruling on the subject, I, for
one, would be glad to pay my rates.
But I do not see why we should
be made the scapegoats of official
inefficiency."

西区被设路障的里弄住宅
处于上海公共租界警务处严密监视之下

提丰路一百多户住宅被禁止进入租界道路；
市政当局阻断污水排放口

住户保持冷静但对此举表示愤慨

由于上海公共租界工部局指导下的市警务处采取果断行动，昨天清晨，提丰路（Tifeng Road）上一百多幢西式住宅的租户被切断了直接进入市政道路的通道。当工务局停止该建筑群落的污水排放后，针对住户采取了进一步的明确行动。

正如《字林西报》昨天上午首先指出的那样，静安寺捕房的警察在工务局苦力的协助下，封锁了提丰路西侧从愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）延伸至静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的几个建筑群的入口。连接这些住宅与提丰路、静安寺路和愚园路的弄堂对所有交通有效关闭。居民要么通过店铺门口进入租界道路，要么沿着房产后方的一条华人拥有的弄堂通行。

在各方面，警方的封锁昨天都行之有效。沉重且特制的木制结构顶部缠绕着高得难以攀爬的铁丝网，横亘在这排建筑的十一个入口处。每个出口都被彻底堵死，并在每个路障处部署警察，以防止内部人员试图强行移除路障或进行其他不轨举动。

区域平静

但整个街区普遍保持安静。那些居住在路障后面的人听天由命，要么通过位于提丰路和愚园路拐角处的几家商店，要么沿着一条从这个小社区后方通向愚园路的狭窄小巷，设法进入租界主干道。

当然，大楼的租户中存在着相当大的愤慨。但是，鉴于封锁是在大多数居民熟睡或在室内时迅速而有效地执行的，因此没有人试图干扰警察或苦力队伍的工作。此外，市政官员曾多次威胁要采取此类性质的行动，因此这对目前受影响的人来说并不感到意外。

昨天天亮后不久，一群工务局工人开始在建筑物通往愚园路的入口处挖掘，并在短时间内切断了该物业通往工部局主污水系统的污水出口。到目前为止，尚未有人尝试或威胁切断电力、供水或电话服务，但如果租户继续顽固不化，目前没有任何保证表明不会采取这些措施。

拒绝付款

工部局针对被封锁区域居民所采取的措施，是由于该区域约105栋房屋的租户持续拒绝缴纳市政捐税。该物业的房屋占用者有义务自行缴纳捐税，这些费用不包含在租金内。只有极少数人支付了这些款项。其余的人则坚持拒绝支付。

工部局被迫采取行动以强制执行其要求，于是计划对整个物业进行封锁，并于昨天清晨付诸实施。在严寒和大雨中，由静安寺捕房和后备队分遣队监护和守卫的中国苦力队，迅速将路障从附近的仓库转移到现址。官员们严守秘密，令该街区措手不及。

然而，曾警告租户，如果他们愿意，可以在规定时间前将汽车移出，但相当多的人认为这不过是工部局的另一种姿态，决定冒险一试。现在他们的汽车无法到达主干道。

警察驻守

整夜及昨天全天，警察分遣队在各入口处执勤。他们将轮流驻守，直到工部局从租户那里得到满意的结果为止。在被封锁区域内，只有几家商店可以直接进入租界道路，这些商店的入口未受影响。许多内部租户正利用这些商店进出被围困区域。

涉案物业官方地址位于愚园路361号，但该物业从愚园路沿提丰路延伸至静安寺路，进深较大。这里有十排三层楼的西式住宅，由足够宽以允许机动车通行的弄堂隔开。正是这些通往提丰路、愚园路和静安寺路的弄堂被封锁了。

提丰路的路障

愚园路361弄的居民昨天早上惊醒时发现，他们所有通往提丰路和静安寺路的弄堂入口均被上海公共租界警务处封锁。这些道路被指定为“市政设施”，工部局认为仅供那些有助于增加市政收入的纳税人使用。上方的照片显示了路障的全景，下方显示了几名执勤警察。[阿芳

在该物业的两端坐落着几家临街店铺。静安寺路上的店铺空置，但愚园路上正对静安寺救火会的店铺正在营业。该物业建于1932年，属华人所有。

无视警告

副司库 V. H. Bourne 先生曾向该地区所有居民发出关于未缴捐税的警告，但被无视。几天前又发出了进一步警告和最后通牒，告知租户除非付款，否则将停止进入市政道路并中断污水系统。

很难知道受影响区域居住着多少人，但昨天获悉那里只有两名外国人居住。

昨天接受询问时，工部局官员 emphatically 表示，在租户缴纳捐税之前，他们不会撤除路障或恢复污水连接。工部局表现出进行无限期围困的决心。另有暗示称，在租界道路上其他拖欠捐税的地区，如有必要，也将采取类似措施。

税务局官员昨晚拒绝透露本案涉及的捐税具体数额，但表示数额巨大。就收入而言，过去几年外部道路的情况每况愈下。越来越多的居民拒绝付款，给工部局造成了巨大损失。

关于控制这些干道并向其上居民征税的争议权利的长期谈判仍无进展。工部局的 Stirling Fessenden 先生与上海市政府的俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui，音译）先生之间的讨论曾达成一项临时协定。但谈判仅止于此。此后寻求摆脱僵局的所有努力均证明徒劳无功。

与此同时，这些道路上的大多数居民在很大程度上逃避了税收，一方面不向中方付款，另一方面拒绝向租界当局付款。

“欠税者”的观点

昨天，提丰路的一位中国居民，一位自认的“欠税者”，向《字林西报》表达的更多的是无奈而非愤慨。“在某种程度上，我们很高兴工部局采取了行动，”他宣称，“因为现在捐税问题应该一劳永逸地解决。”

这位在城市中颇有名气的商人表示，“欠税者”的责任小于有关当局，是当局允许局势发展到目前这种不确定状态。

“一方面，工部局的收税员来找我们，”他解释说，“如果我们不付钱给他们，必然会有不少麻烦。另一方面，中国的收税员也来催缴——如果他们不满意，同样令人不快。

“这意味着，除非我们缴纳双重税款，否则总会以某种方式遇到麻烦，那么在局势明朗之前，谁能责怪我们拒绝付款呢？如果对此事有权威裁决，我个人很乐意缴纳捐税。但我不明白为什么我们要成为官方低效的替罪羊。”

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MARCH 14, 1937
586.3
OPEN LETTER TO
S. M. C.
(The following open letter to the
Shanghai Municipal Council has
been received by THE CHINA PRESS.
—Editor.)
Stirling Fessenden, Esquire,
Secretary-General,
Shanghai Municipal Council.
Dear Sir:—
With reference to your Deputy
Revenue Treasurer's letter of 4th
instant:
informing me that the connection
to the Municipal sewerage and
drainage systems and also
direct access to Yu Yuen Road,
etc., would be withdrawn from all
occupants of the block of proper-
ty served principally by Lane 361
Yu Yuen Road, that this with-
drawal which would take effect
from March 10, 1937 was rendered
necessary by the unwillingness of
a number of occupants to contri-
bute their share of Special Rate,
that, in order to avoid inconveni-
ence to those occupants, such as
myself, who had heretofore re-
gularly paid Special Rate to the
Council, efforts had been made to
persuade the owners of the property
to assume the responsibility for col-
lection and payment of this rate by
incorporating the amount in the
rental, and that as the owners did
not agree to this arrangement, the
Council had no other alternative
but to withdraw the above-men-
tioned amenities:
I regret to say that the Council
had thought fit to resort to the
above drastic measures, which were
put into effect on the 11th instant.
In this connexion, I, being a regu-
lar payer of Special Rate to the
Council and a resident in Lane
361, would like to express my per-
sonal opinion as follows:
(a) As the majority of the ten-
ants in Lane 361 has heretofore re-
gularly paid Special Rate to the
Council, the Council's action in
blockading the tax-payers' access
to the streets and withdrawing the
sewerage and drainage systems from
their premises is most unjustified
and untenable.
(b) When any tenant in the Lane
is unwilling to pay his share of
Special Rate, and if the Council
believes that it has the right to
collect tax on extra roads, the
Council is at liberty to take action
against him through the proper le-
gal channel, viz, the law court, or
to adopt other appropriate mea-
sures, which are in no circumstan-
ces to affect the freedom of, or to
cause trouble to, the payers of
Special Rate in the same lane.
(c) According to THE CHINA
PRESS, today's issue, you pointed
out to one of their reporters that,
inter alia, "it is an issue between
the Council and the tax defaulters".
It is quite clear that this is not
an issue between the Council and
the regular payers of Special Rate!
Then, is it justified to treat the
payers of Special Rate in the same
way as the non-payers?
In view of the above, you are
kindly requested to reconsider the
case for the welfare of the resi-
dents at the above-mentioned place.
Yours faithfully,
(Signed) T. T. CHIEN
March 12, 1937,
83, Lane 361, Yu Yuen Road,
Shanghai.

致工部局的公开信
（《大美晚报》收到以下致上海公共租界工部局的公开信。——编者按。）

Stirling Fessenden 先生，
秘书长，
上海公共租界工部局。

尊敬的先生：—

关于贵局副税务司本月4日的来信：

通知我，由于部分占用者不愿分担特别捐税，位于愚园路361弄主要服务的这一街区物业的所有占用者将被切断与市政污水和排水系统的连接，以及通往愚园路等的直接通道；该切断措施将于1937年3月10日起生效；为了避免给像我这样此前一直定期向工部局缴纳特别捐税的占用者带来不便，曾努力说服物业业主承担收取和支付此捐税的责任，方法是将其纳入租金；由于业主不同意此安排，工部局别无选择，只能撤回上述设施：

我很遗憾地说，工部局认为适宜采取上述严厉措施，这些措施已于本月11日实施。在此方面，作为工部局特别捐税的定期缴纳者和361弄的居民，我想表达我个人意见如下：

(a) 由于361弄的大多数租户此前一直定期向工部局缴纳特别捐税，工部局封锁纳税人进入街道并从其住所切断污水和排水系统的行为是最无正当理由且站不住脚的。

(b) 当弄堂内的任何租户不愿支付其份额的特别捐税时，如果工部局认为有权在额外道路上征税，工部局可以通过适当的法律渠道，即法院，对其采取行动，或采取其他适当措施，在任何情况下都不应影响同一弄堂内特别捐税缴纳者的自由或给他们造成麻烦。

(c) 根据今天《大美晚报》的报道，您向记者指出，其中包括“这是工部局与欠税者之间的问题”。很清楚，这不是工部局与特别捐税定期缴纳者之间的问题！那么，以对待非缴纳者的相同方式对待特别捐税缴纳者是否正当？

鉴于上述情况，恳请您为了上述地点居民的福祉重新考虑此案。

此致
敬礼

（签名）T. T. CHIEN
1937年3月12日，
上海愚园路361弄83号。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MARCH 14, 1937

S.M.C. May
Lift Tax
War Siege

Many Besieged Residents Said Paying Rates

LANDLORDS PLAN
TO OPEN LANE

Chinese Enforce 2 A.M.
Curfew On All
Cabarets

Everything was serene and peaceful on the Shanghai Municipal Council's tax war front last night. Not only that but the report was circulated yesterday that the barricades around the 120 foreign-style houses bordering on Yu Yuen, Tifeng and Bubbling Well Roads, occupied by tenants delinquent in paying their rates, may be removed Monday or Tuesday. Officials of the S.M.C. neither confirmed nor denied the rumor.

THE CHINA PRESS was reliably informed last night that a number of tenants in the besieged area have paid their rates since the barricades were erected Thursday. It is estimated that approximately three-fourths of the residents of the district have paid up, hence the report that the Council intends to remove the obstructions to the entrances of the lanes leading to the houses.

Conditions inside the blockaded area remained practically unchanged last night. Only a few motor-cars are now in the area. Several were let out Thursday while another went out Friday with the permission of the Settlement police. The landlords yesterday discovered another outlet to the street. This adjoins a narrow lane in Chinese-controlled territory and is in close proximity to Bubbling Well Road. Here, the landlord has installed two temporary street lights for the convenience of the tenants.

The landlords stated yesterday that if the Council prolongs the seige, they will proceed with plans to open a new lane leading to ~~Shanghai cemetery~~ in order to allow motor-cars and tenants to leave and enter the zone.

Reports that the tenants in the area who have paid their taxes are seeking legal advice with the idea of suing the Shanghai Municipal Council for damages unless the barricades are removed still persisted. Some of the tenants interviewed stated that the matter had already been taken up with their legal advisers with the idea of seeking redress and that some action might be forthcoming. No really definite statements, however, could be obtained.

In the meantime, the situation in the cabaret zones situated along outside roads, remained unchanged. All cabarets in Chinese territory such as Del Monte's, Farrens, the Jessfield Club and the string of Russian all night establishments along Great Western Roads, are being forced by the Chinese authorities to close their doors at 2 a.m. Thus far, there has been no trouble and the action of the Chinese authorities in this regard has been extended to the cabarets along North Szechuen Road.

《字林西报》，1937年3月14日，星期日

工部局可能
取消捐税
围困战

许多被围居民称已缴纳捐税

房东计划
开辟弄堂

中方强制所有
歌舞厅执行
凌晨两点宵禁

昨晚，上海公共租界工部局的“捐税战”前线一片祥和宁静。不仅如此，昨日还流传着一则消息：围绕在愚园路、地丰路（今乌鲁木齐北路）和静安寺路（今南京西路）沿线、由拖欠捐税的租户居住的120幢西式房屋周围的街垒，可能会于周一或周二拆除。工部局官员既未证实也未否认这一谣言。

据《字林西报》昨晚从可靠渠道获悉，自周四设立街垒以来，被围困区域内的一些租户已经缴纳了捐税。据估计，该地区约四分之三的居民已缴清欠款，因此有消息称工部局打算移除通往这些房屋的弄堂入口处的障碍物。

昨晚，封锁区内的情况基本没有变化。目前区域内只有几辆汽车。其中几辆是在周四放行的，另一辆则在周五经租界警方许可后驶出。房东们昨天发现了另一个通向街道的出口。该出口毗邻华界的一条狭窄弄堂，且靠近静安寺路。在此处，房东为方便租户安装了两盏临时路灯。

房东们昨天表示，如果工部局延长围困时间，他们将着手实施开辟一条通往~~上海公墓~~的新弄堂的计划，以便让汽车和租户进出该区域。

有关该地区已纳税租户正在寻求法律建议、拟除非拆除街垒否则将起诉上海公共租界工部局要求赔偿的报道仍在持续。一些接受采访的租户表示，此事已与其法律顾问接洽，旨在寻求补救，并可能会有所行动。然而，未能获得任何真正明确的声明。

与此同时，位于越界筑路区域的歌舞厅情况保持不变。华界的所有歌舞厅，如德尔蒙特（Del Monte's）、法伦斯（Farrens）、杰司菲尔德俱乐部（Jessfield Club）以及大西路（今延安西路）沿线的一排俄式通宵营业场所，均被中国当局强制要求在凌晨2点关门。截至目前，尚未发生任何冲突，中国当局在此方面的行动已扩展至北四川路沿线的歌舞厅。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, MARCH 14, 1937

OUTSIDE ROADS
S.M.C.'s Right to Acquire
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—A number of uncontradicted
assertions have been made in Shang-
hai newspapers contending that the
Shanghai Municipal Council have
no rights outside the limits of the
Foreign Settlement (and presumably
the French Municipal Council also).
The Settlement is governed by the
"Land Regulations," which were
mutually agreed upon by the Chi-
nese Government and the Foreign
Ministers in China at the time they
were made effective. Until they are
superseded by some other form of
government, or the refusal of one of
the parties to carry out the agree-
ment they have made, or war, they
remain the only basis of government
to-day. Land Regulation VI reads
as follows:—
It shall also be lawful for the Land
Renters, and others who may be
entitled to vote as hereinafter men-
tioned, in public meeting assembled,
to purchase land leading or being out
of the Settlement, or to accept land
from foreign or native owners upon
terms to be mutually agreed upon
between the Council and such for-
eign or native owners, for the purpose
of converting the same into roads or
public gardens and places of recrea-
tion and amusement, and it shall be
lawful for the Council from time to
time to apply such portion of the
funds raised under Article IX of these
Regulations, for the purchase, crea-
tion and maintenance of such roads,
gardens, etc., as may be necessary
and expedient.
The S.M.C. has purchased the land
on which outside roads are made and
paid for it. Article IX empowers
them to collect rates and taxes for
the upkeep of the roads. The same
Land Regulation states that "such
roads shall be dedicated to the public
use....of all persons residing within
the Settlement." The occupants with-
in the present "distressed area" of
Tifeng Road do not reside within the
Settlement, so the S.M.C. ask them
to contribute to the roads on which
their houses are built—or refrain
from using them.
GREAT WESTERN.
Shanghai, March 13.
page_data.zh:
《字林西报》，1937年3月14日，星期日

越界筑路
工部局的征购权
致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，——上海多家报纸发表了一些未经反驳的断言，声称上海公共租界工部局在外国租界范围之外（推测法国公董局亦然）没有任何权利。租界受《土地章程》管辖，该章程在其生效时由中国政府与驻华外国公使共同商定。除非被其他形式的政府所取代，或一方拒绝履行已达成的协议，或发生战争，否则它们仍是当今唯一的治理基础。《土地章程》第六条规定如下：

凡承租人及下文所述其他享有投票权者，在公开集会上，亦有权购买通向租界外或位于租界外的土地，或按工部局与此类外籍或华人业主相互商定的条款，接受外籍或华人业主的土地，目的是将其改建为道路、公园及娱乐休闲场所；工部局亦有权不时动用根据本章程第九条筹集的资金中的一部分，用于购买、建造和维护此类必要的且适宜的道路、花园等。

工部局已购买并支付了修建越界筑路所需的土地费用。第九条授权其征收捐税以维护道路。同一《土地章程》规定，“此类道路应供公众使用……供所有居住在租界内的人士使用。” 目前地丰路“受困区域”内的居住者并不居住在租界内，因此工部局要求他们为其房屋所建的道路做出贡献，或者禁止使用这些道路。

GREAT WESTERN.
上海，3月13日。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MARCH 14, 1937

'STUPID VALLEY' WILL
HAVE NEW OUTLET

Landlord Threatens To
Demolish Houses For
Back-Door Exit

BESEIGED VILLAGE
CONTINUES QUIET

The beseiged village of "Stupid Valley"—the alleyway in Yu Yuen Road extra-settlement territory which was barricaded by the S.M.C. on Wednesday night because of the failure of some of the tenants to pay taxes—quietly carried on business yesterday regardless of the blockade at either end of the street and police patrols.

After three days of the strange situation there was no evidence that tenants had decided to pay their rates. Instead it was stated in reliable Chinese sources that the landlords affected were seeking to open a new alleyway into Chinese territory. Three houses will have to be torn down to accomplish this, but the owner has declared himself willing to make the sacrifice and a petition to this effect has been sent to the authorities of the Shanghai City Government.

Rumours, which could not be confirmed through the Council, stated that many tenants had paid their rates since the blockade, bringing the total of those who have paid to nearly three-quarters of the residents. If this is true, it is believed likely that the blockade may be removed by Monday.

Only a few motor cars are still inside the blockaded area. Several were let out on Thursday and another one was allowed to pass on Friday afternoon. The owner of this car was visiting a friend when the barricade was put up and did not get out in time. He convinced the Council authorities that he was not a resident of the alleyway and was thus permitted to drive his car away.
page_data.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1937年3月14日

“愚谷”将拥有
新出口

房东威胁拆除房屋
以开辟后门出口

被围村庄
继续保持平静

“愚谷”——这个位于愚园路越界筑路区域的弄堂，因部分租户未能缴纳税款，于周三晚被工部局设置街垒封锁——尽管街道两端设有路障且有警察巡逻，昨日仍平静地照常进行日常活动。

在这种奇怪的局面持续三天后，没有证据表明租户已决定缴纳捐税。相反，据可靠的中文消息来源称，受影响的房东正试图开辟一条通往华界的新弄堂。为此必须拆除三栋房屋，但业主已表示愿意做出这一牺牲，并已向上海市政府当局提交了以此为目的的请愿书。

虽有谣言称，自封锁以来许多租户已缴纳捐税，使已缴费人数接近居民总数的四分之三，但这些说法无法通过工部局得到证实。如果属实，人们认为封锁可能会在周一解除。

封锁区内目前仅剩几辆汽车。几辆车于周四获准驶出，另一辆车于周五下午获准通行。该车车主在设置路障时正在拜访朋友，未能及时离开。他向工部局当局说服自己并非该弄堂的常住居民，从而获准驾车离开。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, March 13, 1937

Wise Or Otherwise?
IF THIS were a world where black were always black and white always white, we would feel the Shanghai Municipal Council not only justified but wise in taking drastic action against certain dwellers off extra-Settlement roads who have not paid their Settlement rates.
But there are complexities in this world of ours, many things in which botd blacks and whites shade off into grays, and we are smitten with doubts as to the full advisability of this step at this time. Specifically, we think the Council will win on this issue but that it may find it has achieved a Pyrrhic victory.
On at least two points the Council seems to us to be definitely in the wrong. One is with reference to such dwellers in the affected area as have duly paid municipal rates. If a single person has, that person is being subjected to unfair treatment; and the assertion is being made that an appreciable number have so paid. The other is with reference to motorcars impounded although their owners have paid the regular license fees. On both these points the Council appears to have laid itself open to criticism, possible legal action and certainly a vast deal of general resentment with possibly far reaching political consequences.
However, it is strictly up to the Council to judge whether it is likely to get itself into more political hot water than its skin can stand. We agree that the people who are now being subjected to inconvenience should not be allowed to go on indefinitely dodging the payment of taxes to both foreign and Chinese authorities. Our sole doubt is to whether there has not been a bit of the bull-in-china-shop about all this, which perhaps might have been avoided.
There is sufficient vagueness about the Land Regulations' very provision of Outside Roads in the first place. Administrative rights have been debated for years, there being no specific provision. The right to tax occupants of premises abutting on the Outside Roads is assumed but unstated. Finally—a long but necessary mental jump—if foreigners can be "tough" about taxing Chinese...
On one thusfar little regarded but to us very vital detail we feel that the Council has shown the most complete unwisdom. That is in the matter of publicity concerning the precise status of the whole Outside Roads position. Why must any such situation as the present one come to pass What have the Japanese been demanding which blocked agreement on the Outside Roads issue at a time when virtually all other Sino-foreign relations have been more amicable, when there has been more complete understanding, than at any time in history? The public deserves to know. To let the light of day into the dark corners of this subject, far from doing harm, might well prove the best possible way to move toward an understanding.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月13日，星期六

明智与否？

如果这是一个黑即是黑、白即是白的世界，我们会觉得上海公共租界工部局对某些居住在越界筑路区域且未缴纳租界捐税的居民采取严厉行动，不仅是正当的，而且是明智的。

但我们的世界充满复杂性，许多事情中黑与白都渐变为灰色，我们不禁对此时采取这一步骤的完全妥当性产生怀疑。具体而言，我们认为工部局将在这一问题上获胜，但可能会发现其取得的是一场皮洛士式的胜利（惨胜）。

至少在两点上，工部局在我们看来显然是错误的。一点是关于受影响区域内那些已按规定缴纳市政捐税的居民。如果有一人如此，则该人正遭受不公平待遇；且有说法称已有相当数量的人如此缴纳。另一点是关于虽已缴纳常规牌照费但仍被扣押的汽车。在这两点上，工部局似乎使自己面临批评、可能的法律诉讼，以及肯定会产生大量的普遍怨恨，这可能带来深远的政治后果。

然而，判断是否可能陷入超出其承受能力的政治困境，严格来说取决于工部局自身。我们同意，不应允许目前遭受不便的人们无限期地逃避向外国和中国当局缴纳税款。我们唯一的疑虑是，这一切是否带有一点“鲁莽闯祸”（bull-in-china-shop）的色彩，而这或许本可以避免。

首先，《土地章程》中关于越界筑路的规定本身就存在足够的模糊性。行政管理权多年来一直存在争议，因为没有具体规定。对毗邻越界筑路的房产 occupant（居住者/占用者）征税的权利是假定的，但未明文规定。最后——这是一个漫长但必要的思维跳跃——如果外国人可以在向中国人征税问题上表现得“强硬”……

在一个迄今为止很少被关注但对我们至关重要的细节上，我们认为工部局表现出了最彻底的不明智。那就是关于整个越界筑路地位确切状况的 publicity（宣传/公开信息）。为什么会出现目前的这种局面？在日本方面提出了什么要求，导致在几乎所有其他中外关系都比历史上任何时候更加友好、理解更为全面的时期，却在越界筑路问题上阻碍了协议的达成？公众有权知道。让阳光照进这一主题的黑暗角落，非但不会造成伤害，反而可能被证明是走向理解的最佳途径。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, March 13, 1937

Stupid Valley
Front All Quiet
In Tax Battle

Siege Of House-Block
Ending Third Day;
Many Pay Rates

BARRIER REMOVAL
EXPECTED MONDAY

City Government Said
Planning Counter
Measures

All was quiet this morning on the "Stupid Valley" front of the Shanghai Municipal Council-tenant "tax war." The siege of the half block of 120 three-story, foreign-style houses bordering Bubbling Well, Tifeng and Yu Yuen Roads, entered the third day today with prospects of an early solution still uncertain.

Rumors were circulated this morning that many tenants have paid their rates—12 per cent of their monthly rent—since the blockade, bringing the total of tenants who have paid to three-fourths of the population there, and that the barricades, erected Thursday, will be removed on Monday. These rumors, however, could not be confirmed. Council officials today refused to reveal the number of tenants who have already paid their rates and to reveal the date when the barricades are to be removed.

Conditions Unchanged

Conditions inside the besieged compound remain unchanged this morning. The landlords, having found another outlet adjoining a narrow lane in the Chinese controlled territory in close proximity of Bubbling Well Road, have installed two temporary street lights for the convenience of the tenants. "We will continue our fight at any cost," the rent agent declared this morning. "If the Council is to prolong the siege, we will proceed with our plans to open a new alleyway leading to Chinese territory to allow motor cars to enter and leave our lane."

Some of the tenants inside the besieged "city" declare that the Police Bureau of the City Government is seriously considering drastic counter-measures to remove the barricades. This is unlikely in view of the statement issued by Mr. O. K. Yui, secretary-general of the City Government, who, while expressing his regret at the incident, advised the tenants to pay "compensation" to the Council, through the City Government, if necessary, for their use of the Council sewer and drainage facilities.

Car Let Out

Only a few motor-cars are now inside the blockaded village. While several were let out on Thursday afternoon, another one was allowed to pass yesterday afternoon. The owner of the car was visiting a friend when the last exit of the lane on Yu Yuen Road was blocked on Thursday morning. By convincing the Council officials that he is not a resident of the alleyway and that he has fulfilled all of his obligations to the Council, he obtained special permission to drive the car away from the besieged "city."

The blockade outside a Tifeng Road exit was specially lifted for him by a group of Public Works Department coolies at the command of the Bubbling Well Station. He drove the car out triumphantly after having been deprived of the title as a motorist for some 30 hours.

Meanwhile, tenants who have been paying the municipal rates before the blockade are complaining to the Council for its alleged failure to show discrimination in taking the drastic action. It is said that they are seeking legal advice with a view to seeking redress against the Council in the Court of Consuls. The attitude towards the Council action is disclosed in a letter addressed to Mr. Stirling Fessenden, secretary-general of the Council, by Mr. T M. Chen, tenant of House 83 "Stupid Valley" village.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月13日，星期六

愚园路
前线平静
税务战

街区围困
进入第三天；
多人缴纳税捐

预计周一
拆除路障

据称市政府
正筹划反制
措施

在上海公共租界工部局与租户的“税务战”中，“愚园路”前线今晨一片平静。对毗邻静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）、提丰路（Tifeng Road）和愚园路（Yu Yuen Road）的半排共120幢三层西式住宅的围困，今日已进入第三天，能否早日解决仍不确定。

今晨有谣言流传，称自封锁以来，许多租户已缴纳了税捐——即其月租金的百分之十二，使得已缴纳税捐的租户占总人数的四分之三；另有传言称，周四设立的路障将于周一拆除。然而，这些谣言未能得到证实。工部局官员今日拒绝透露已缴纳税捐的租户人数，也拒绝透露路障将于何时拆除。

状况未变

今晨，被围困街区内的状况保持不变。房东们在靠近静安寺路、位于华界的一条狭窄弄堂旁找到了另一个出口，并安装了两盏临时路灯以方便租户。“我们将不惜一切代价继续斗争，”租赁代理人今晨宣称。“如果工部局延长围困，我们将执行计划，开辟一条通往华界的新弄堂，以便汽车进出我们的里弄。”

一些被困在“城”内的租户声称，市政府警察局正在认真考虑采取严厉的反制措施以拆除路障。鉴于市政府秘书长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）先生发表的声明，这种情况不太可能发生。俞先生在对该事件表示遗憾的同时，建议租户如有必要，通过市政府向工部局支付“补偿金”，以使用工部局的下水道和排水设施。

车辆获准驶出

目前只有几辆汽车留在被封锁的街区内。虽然有几辆车在周四下午被放行，但另一辆车是在昨天下午获准通过的。该车车主在周四早晨愚园路上该弄堂的最后一个出口被封锁时，正在拜访朋友。通过说服工部局官员，证明他并非该弄堂的住户，且已履行对工部局的所有义务，他获得了特别许可，将汽车驶离被围困的“城”。

在静安寺捕房指挥下，一组工务局苦力专门为他移除了提丰路出口处的路障。在被剥夺驾驶者身份约30小时后，他得意洋洋地驾车驶出。

与此同时，那些在封锁前一直缴纳市政税捐的租户正向工部局投诉，指责其在采取严厉行动时未能区别对待。据说，他们正在寻求法律建议，旨在向领事法庭起诉工部局以求补救。陈T M.（T M. Chen）先生在一封致工部局总办费信惇（Stirling Fessenden）先生的信中，披露了对工部局行动的态度。陈先生是“愚园路”村83号房屋的租户。

enkitied £0 vi 7 as pereinasier : mer:

from foreign or native owners upon 
terms to be mutually agreed upon 
between the Council and such for- 
eign or native owners, for the purpose 
of converting the same into roads or 
public gardens and places of recrea- 
tion ami amusement, and it shall be 
Jawful for the Council from time te 
time to apply such 
funds r. under Article IX of these 
Regulations, for the purchase, crea- 
tion and maintenance of such roads, 
gardens, etc., as may be necessary 
and expedient. .

paid for it. Article IX empowers 
them to .collect rates and taxes for

roads shall be dedicated to the ‘public
